site.$comment_platforms: Third-party platform names banned on the public storefront (F-2c C-4 / ADR-M004 D14): product wiring is described generically ('a lending venue', 'a perp DEX'), never by a partner/protocol brand. Unambiguous brands use a plain \b word boundary. UMA and Gamma carry a STRICT \b...\b boundary so substrings (human, summary, Pendleton) do not false-positive; note the gate compiles case-insensitive, so the standalone options-greek word 'gamma' in prose WOULD match — a known limit alongside the ambiguous 'Safe' (deliberately NOT listed: it is a common English word AND a multisig brand; manual review per lot). Adding a name = this ADR line. Verified by a mutant test.

harness.$comment: (ADR-M005 D9 / K-3): apps/harness sources + tool descriptions scanned for honesty vocab NOT in the GLOBAL list. 'confidence' is load-bearing (fleet invariant: no confidence field/score anywhere) — the mission's named example, and what harness_tool_descriptions_pass_vocab kills. 'autonomous'/'self-evolving' mirror the site honesty subset and carry no legitimate use in a coverage-gate server. Then (ADR-M007 D5/B-3): the calibrate surface must police 'guarantees'/'predicts'/'probative' NEGATION-AWARE, so the honest existing negations stay green: 'no guarantee'/'no score' (cascade/attest), 'not probative'/'no probative'/'attest_makes_no_probative_claim' (attest, schema-projection), and 'not a measured predictor' (only 'predicts' is banned, never 'predictor'). A naked surclaim ('guarantees coverage'/'the scores are probative'/'MONARK predicts ...') reddens. Both 'no' and 'not' are negations; the '[\s_]' separator covers the snake_case identifier. Adding a name = this ADR line.

naked "guarantee/guarantees/guaranteed" surclaim on the calibrate surface; the honest "no guarantee" stays green (ADR-M007 B-3 ; R1: ADR-literal — participle covered, so "coverage is guaranteed" reddens. Known limit: "not/cannot guaranteed" would also redden — no such honest span exists in scope; a future one = an exemptPhrases line)
naked "probative" surclaim; the honest "not probative"/"no probative"/"no_probative" negations stay green (ADR-M007 B-3)

skills.$comment: (ADR-M006 D2/D5): the ClawHub skill artefacts under skills/ (SKILL.md, INTEGRATION.md, ...) carry the honesty framing, so the SAME negation-aware overclaim gate the harness applies to its tool surface applies here — PLUS the securities vocabulary (ADR-M006 M-2, kept OUT of the skill: profit-share/yield/APY/pay-for-inference/staking) and the risk #1 mis-read of the coverage gate as a spend guard (ADR-M006 D2). The pattern 'spend[-\s]?(cap|guard|limit)' catches the mis-read, while 'spend controls' (the honest pointer to the caller's own platform) stays green; the ONE honest sentence that names '$/token spend cap' only to DENY it is masked by the closed exemptPhrases below (same closed-list mechanism as the site scope). 'live'/'proven' (ADR-M006 M-9) never describe the skill. No naked '\bBTC\b' ban here on purpose: the committed class 'btc-dir-15m' (D9/C-3) is a mandated, disclosed plumbing fixture. Adding a pattern = this ADR line.
